- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; apply downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or 1.5x prior 14-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >1.2x recent 14-day average, reduce by 15–25%.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and forecast is high, model is prone to overconfidence — apply 5–10% downward adjustment to all 30d values.
- Forecast errors cluster in the last 5–7 days of 30d horizon — adjust downward for final 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
